notes: TEXTBOOK: For 2026-27 Class X still uses the rationalised NCERT 'Mathematics: Textbook for Class X' (14 chapters; Constructions removed). NCERT said in March 2026 that new NCF-SE books for Grades 10 and 11 come only from 2027-28; I read this in news reports because the NCERT advisory PDF is blocked to the fetch tool.

STANDARD vs BASIC: CBSE offers Mathematics Standard (041) and Mathematics Basic (241). They have the same syllabus, the same textbook and the same 80+20 mark structure; only the question-paper design differs. Standard: Remembering/Understanding 43 marks (54%), Applying 19 (24%), Analysing/Evaluating/Creating 18 (22%). Basic: 60 (75%), 12 (15%), 8 (10%). This file covers both; no outcome is Standard-only.

UNIT WEIGHTS (theory 80 marks, 3 hours): Number Systems 6, Algebra 20, Coordinate Geometry 6, Geometry 15, Trigonometry 12, Mensuration 10, Statistics and Probability 11. Internal assessment 20: pen-paper test and multiple assessment 10 (5+5), portfolio 5, lab practical 5. The extracted text of the 2026-27 document gave no period counts.

PROOFS CBSE REQUIRES (assessment human): irrationality of sqrt 2, sqrt 3, sqrt 5 and numbers like 3 + 2 sqrt 5; the Basic Proportionality Theorem; the tangent at a point is perpendicular to the radius; tangents from an external point are equal; sin^2 A + cos^2 A = 1 and simple identities; that the trigonometric ratios of an acute angle are well defined. Converse of BPT and the similarity criteria are stated without proof and only applied.

RESTRICTIONS stated by CBSE: quadratic equations only with real roots, by factorisation and the quadratic formula; section formula for internal division only; heights and distances with at most two right triangles and angles of 30, 45 and 60 degrees; segment areas only for central angles of 60, 90 and 120 degrees; surface area and volume for combinations of any two of cube, cuboid, sphere, hemisphere, right circular cylinder and cone; grouped mean by direct, assumed-mean and step-deviation methods; median and mode of grouped data without bimodal cases; probability by the classical definition only.

DELETED (rationalised since 2023-24; not in the 2026-27 syllabus): Euclid's division lemma; decimal expansions of rationals; division algorithm for polynomials; cross-multiplication and equations reducible to linear pairs; completing the square; areas of similar triangles; Pythagoras theorem (Ch 6); area of a triangle in coordinates; trigonometric ratios of complementary angles; Constructions chapter; review of circle perimeter/area and combinations of plane figures; conversion of solids and the frustum; ogives. This list comes from a secondary site (pw.live) and is consistent with the official syllabus topics; there is no official deletion list in the 2026-27 document.

SECTIONS: section headings were checked on SATHEE (IIT Kanpur's mirror of the NCERT text) for Chs 3, 8, 9, 11 and 13. For Chs 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 10, 12 and 14 those pages would not load; their headings are the known rationalised-edition headings and fit the deleted-sections list, but I could not check them against the print in this session.

CHAPTER TITLES: all 14 titles appear in the SATHEE listing. Most also match the CBSE 2026-27 topic headings (official). 'Some Applications of Trigonometry' appears in CBSE only as the topic 'Heights and Distances'; CBSE also lists 'Trigonometric Identities' as a separate topic, which in the book is Section 8.4 of Ch 8. All chapters are marked verified:true on the basis of the CBSE and SATHEE sources together.

EXAM SCHEME: the 2026-27 curriculum document describes a single 80-mark, 3-hour theory paper. The two-board-examination arrangement for Class X (main exam plus an optional second exam) is not described in this document and was not verified here.
CH 2: CBSE restricts the zeros-coefficients relationship to quadratic polynomials. The book also mentions cubic polynomials, but they are not assessed.

outcomes.statement: Express a natural number as a product of primes and state the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic (uniqueness of prime factorisation).
Find the HCF and LCM of numbers from their prime factorisations, use HCF x LCM = product for two numbers, and solve word problems with them.
Use uniqueness of prime factorisation to justify number facts, e.g. that 6^n can never end in 0.
Prove by contradiction that sqrt 2, sqrt 3 and sqrt 5 are irrational, using the fact that if a prime divides a^2 it divides a.

chapters.title: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables

sections.title: Graphical Method of Solution of a Pair of Linear Equations
Algebraic Methods of Solving a Pair of Linear Equations

outcomes.statement: Represent a situation as a pair of linear equations in two variables.
Solve a pair of linear equations graphically and interpret intersecting, parallel and coincident lines.
Decide from the coefficient ratios a1/a2, b1/b2, c1/c2 whether a pair has one, none or infinitely many solutions, and find parameter values for a given case.
Solve a pair of linear equations by substitution.
Solve a pair of linear equations by elimination.
Model and solve everyday problems (ages, money, speeds, digits, geometry) with a pair of linear equations and interpret the solution.

sections.title: Solution of a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation

outcomes.statement: Recognise quadratic equations in standard form ax^2 + bx + c = 0 (a not 0) and form them from situations.
Solve quadratic equations by factorisation (splitting the middle term).
Solve quadratic equations with real roots using the quadratic formula.
Use the discriminant to decide the nature of roots and find parameter values for equal or real roots.
Model everyday problems (areas, speeds, ages, numbers) with quadratic equations, solve them and reject solutions that do not fit the context.

sections.title: Sum of First n Terms of an AP

outcomes.statement: Decide whether a list is an AP and identify its first term and common difference.
Derive and use the nth-term formula of an AP, including the nth term from the end and which term has a given value.
Derive and use the formula for the sum of the first n terms of an AP.
Solve everyday problems (savings, instalments, arrangements) with AP terms and sums.
Explain when figures are similar versus congruent, with examples and counterexamples (e.g. polygons with equal angles but sides not in proportion).
Prove the Basic Proportionality Theorem: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio.
Use the BPT and its converse to find lengths and to show lines are parallel.
Apply the AA/AAA, SSS and SAS similarity criteria to find unknown sides and angles.
Prove triangles similar and deduce relations between their sides, such as equal products of segments.
Calculate the distance between two points with the distance formula.
Use distances to test collinearity, classify triangles and quadrilaterals, and find points equidistant from given points.
Find the point dividing a segment internally in a given ratio, including the midpoint and points of trisection.
Find the ratio in which a point or an axis divides a segment, and unknown vertices (e.g. of a parallelogram) using the section formula.

sections.title: Trigonometric Ratios of Some Specific Angles

outcomes.statement: Define the six trigonometric ratios of an acute angle in a right triangle and explain, using similarity, why they depend only on the angle.
Find the other trigonometric ratios of an angle from one given ratio.
Recall and justify the ratios of 30, 45 and 60 degrees (and the motivated values at 0 and 90), and evaluate expressions with them.
Prove sin^2 A + cos^2 A = 1 and the related identities with sec/tan and cosec/cot.
Prove simple trigonometric identities and simplify expressions using the basic identities.
Identify angles of elevation and depression and draw a labelled diagram for a heights-and-distances situation.
Find heights or distances with one right triangle and angles of 30, 45 or 60 degrees.
Solve heights-and-distances problems involving two right triangles (e.g. two observation points, an object seen from a height).

sections.title: Number of Tangents from a Point on a Circle

outcomes.statement: Tell tangents, secants and non-intersecting lines apart and state how many tangents can be drawn from a point inside, on or outside a circle.
Prove that the tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.
Prove that the two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal in length.
Use tangent properties to find lengths and angles and to prove results such as AB + CD = AD + BC for a quadrilateral circumscribing a circle.

sections.title: Areas of Sector and Segment of a Circle

outcomes.statement: Calculate the area of a sector and the length of its arc from the radius and central angle.
Calculate the area of a segment of a circle for central angles of 60, 90 or 120 degrees.
Solve applied problems with sectors and segments, such as clock hands, wipers and designs.

sections.title: Surface Area of a Combination of Solids
Volume of a Combination of Solids

outcomes.statement: Calculate the surface area of a solid made of two basic solids (cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone, sphere, hemisphere), deciding which faces stay exposed.
Calculate the volume of a solid made of two basic solids.
Model real objects (toys, tents, capsules, vessels) as combinations of solids and answer questions about material or capacity.
Calculate the mean of grouped data by the direct, assumed-mean and step-deviation methods.
Calculate the mode of grouped data from the modal class with the formula.
Calculate the median of grouped data using cumulative frequencies and the median formula.
Find a missing frequency from a given mean or median and interpret which measure of centre suits a situation.
Calculate theoretical (classical) probabilities for experiments with equally likely outcomes, such as coins, dice, cards and balls in bags.
Use the facts that P(E) + P(not E) = 1, that 0 <= P(E) <= 1, and that impossible and sure events have probabilities 0 and 1.
List the sample space of two-stage experiments (two coins, two dice) and find probabilities of events defined on it.
